q: Plants use carbon dioxide and water in the presence of chlorophyll and light to compose _____ and oxygen.
e: Photosynthesis is the process where plants use carbon dioxide and water in the presence of chlorophyll and light to compose glucose and oxygen.

q: Photosynthesis takes place in the _____ of the green parts of plants but mainly in the leaves.
e: Photosynthesis takes place in the chloroplasts of the green parts of plants, but mainly in the leaves.

q: For photosynthesis efficiency, leaves need to have a large surface area to absorb light, much chlorophyll to catch the light, and veins including _____ to supply water.
e: Leaves need veins including xylem and phloem to supply water and carry away photosynthetic products.

q: Most leaves are thin, flat structures supported by _____ which support the leaf blade to be angled to receive the maximum amount of sunlight.
e: Most leaves are thin, flat structures supported by the petiole, which supports the leaf blade to receive maximum sunlight.

q: In many plants, there is a thin waxy layer called the _____ over the epidermis.
e: In many plants, there is a thin waxy layer called the cuticle over the epidermis to reduce water loss.

q: In most dicotyledonous plants, the stomata occur only in the _____.
e: In most dicotyledonous plants, the stomata occur only in the lower epidermis.

q: In monocotyledonous plants, the stomata are _____ distributed on both surfaces of the leaf.
e: In monocotyledonous plants, the stomata are equally distributed on both surfaces of the leaf.

q: The tissue between the upper and lower epidermis is called _____.
e: The tissue between the upper and lower epidermis is called the mesophyll.

q: The palisade mesophyll cells are usually long and contain many _____.
e: The palisade mesophyll cells are usually long and contain many chloroplasts for photosynthesis.

q: The spongy mesophyll cells vary in shape and are loosely arranged with many _____ between them.
e: The spongy mesophyll cells are loosely arranged with many air spaces between them to allow diffusion of gases.

q: The major vein of the leaf is called the _____ continuation of petiole.
e: The major vein of the leaf is called the midrib, which is a continuation of the petiole.

q: In xylem, vessels are cylindrical, hollow and _____ cells.
e: In xylem, vessels are cylindrical, hollow and thick walled cells.

q: The phloem consists of sieve tubes which are elongated cells and the transverse walls of sieve tubes are perforated _____.
e: The transverse walls of sieve tubes in the phloem are perforated sieve plates.

q: The epidermal cells are thin to allow light to pass through and _____ are absent.
e: Epidermal cells are thin to allow light to pass through, and chloroplasts are absent in the upper epidermis.

q: The _____ helps to keep the leaf's shape and to reduce water loss, acting as a barrier to disease organisms.
e: The upper epidermis helps to keep the leaf's shape, reduce water loss, and act as a barrier to disease organisms.

q: The _____ allows diffusion of carbon dioxide and oxygen in and out of mesophyll cells.
e: The spongy mesophyll allows diffusion of carbon dioxide and oxygen in and out of mesophyll cells.

q: Xylem carries water and minerals absorbed by _____ to leaves.
e: Xylem carries water and minerals absorbed by roots to the leaves.

q: Phloem transports photosynthetic products to _____ of the plant.
e: Phloem transports photosynthetic products to other parts of the plant.

q: The stoma is the site of _____ into and out of the leaf.
e: The stoma is the site of gaseous exchange into and out of the leaf.

q: Chloroplast is a membrane bound organelle containing chlorophyll a, b and _____.
e: Chloroplast is a membrane bound organelle containing chlorophyll a, b and other pigments.

q: Chloroplasts found in higher plants are generally _____ shaped.
e: Chloroplasts found in higher plants are generally biconvex shaped.

q: The outer membrane of chloroplast is a semi-porous membrane and is permeable to _____ which diffuse easily.
e: The outer membrane is semi-porous and permeable to small molecules and ions which diffuse easily.

q: The intermembrane space is a thin space about _____ and it lies between the outer and the inner membranes of the chloroplast.
e: The intermembrane space is a thin space about 10-20 nm.

q: The inner membrane of the chloroplast forms a border to the _____ and regulates passage of materials.
e: The inner membrane of the chloroplast forms a border to the stroma and regulates passage of materials.

q: The _____ is the site for the dark reaction of photosynthesis.
e: The stroma is the site for the dark reaction of photosynthesis.

q: The thylakoids are suspended in the stroma and are membranous sacs which are arranged in stacks known as _____.
e: Thylakoids are arranged in stacks known as grana.

q: Each granum contains around _____ thylakoids.
e: Each granum contains around 10-20 thylakoids.

q: The thylakoid membrane is the site for the _____ of photosynthesis.
e: The thylakoid membrane is the site for the light reactions of photosynthesis.

q: Chlorophyll reflects mostly the _____ portion of light.
e: Chlorophyll reflects mostly the green portion of light, which is why plants appear green.

q: The wavelengths of light almost totally absorbed by chlorophyll are blue (480 nm) and _____.
e: Chlorophyll almost totally absorbs blue (480 nm) and red (700 nm) wavelengths of light.

q: Photosynthesis comprises of two phases: the light reaction and the _____.
e: Photosynthesis comprises two phases: the light reaction and the dark reaction.

q: The light reaction takes place on the _____ of chloroplast.
e: The light reaction takes place on the thylakoid membrane of the chloroplast.

q: The dark reaction takes place in the _____ of the chloroplast.
e: The dark reaction takes place in the stroma of the chloroplast.

q: The light reaction is a light-dependent process which includes light absorption, photolysis and release of oxygen and formation of chemical compounds: ATP and _____.
e: The light reaction forms chemical compounds ATP and NADPH.

q: The dark reaction is also called _____.
e: The dark reaction is also called the Calvin cycle.

q: The dark reaction is a light-independent process in which sugar molecules are formed by using carbon dioxide with the help of ATP and _____ produced from the light reaction.
e: The dark reaction uses carbon dioxide with the help of ATP and NADPH produced from the light reaction.

q: In the light reaction, the water molecules split into hydrogen and _____.
e: During the light reaction, water molecules split into hydrogen and oxygen (photolysis).

q: In the dark reaction, glucose molecules are formed using _____.
e: In the dark reaction, glucose molecules are formed using CO2.

q: Photolysis occurs in the light reaction and _____ in the dark reaction.
e: Photolysis occurs in the light reaction and does not occur in the dark reaction.

q: As the light intensity increases, the rate of photosynthesis increases until it reaches a _____.
e: As light intensity increases, the rate of photosynthesis increases until it reaches a maximum rate.

q: Under bright light, the rate of photosynthesis increases with a rise in temperature up to a maximum temperature of around _____.
e: Under bright light, the rate of photosynthesis increases up to a maximum temperature of around 40°C.

q: Beyond the maximum temperature, the rate of photosynthesis drops _____.
e: Beyond the maximum temperature of around 40°C, the rate of photosynthesis drops rapidly.

q: The concentration of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere is about _____.
e: The concentration of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere is about 0.04%.

q: There are four requirements of photosynthesis, namely chlorophyll, light, carbon dioxide and _____.
e: The four requirements of photosynthesis are chlorophyll, light, carbon dioxide, and water.

q: In each investigation for requirements of photosynthesis, the plants must first be _____.
e: In each investigation, the plants must first be destarched to ensure accurate results.

q: The leaves are destarched by placing this plant in the dark for _____.
e: The leaves are destarched by placing the plant in the dark for 2-3 days.

q: Variegated leaves which have chlorophyll as green patches can be found in plants like Coleus, spiderwort and _____.
e: Variegated leaves can be found in plants like Coleus, spiderwort, and croton.

q: Only the green patches previously will turn _____ with iodine solution.
e: Only the green patches containing chlorophyll will turn blue-black with iodine solution, indicating starch presence.

q: In the investigation to show that light is essential, a portion of green leaf is sandwiched between two pieces of black paper or black tape or _____.
e: A portion of the leaf is sandwiched between black paper, black tape, or aluminium foil to block light.

q: In the investigation for carbon dioxide, NaHCO3 is put inside set-up A for producing carbon dioxide and _____ inside set-up B to absorb carbon dioxide.
e: NaOH (sodium hydroxide) is used inside set-up B to absorb carbon dioxide.

q: Leaf from the plant in which NaOH has been placed will stain _____.
e: The leaf from the plant in which NaOH has been placed will stain brown, indicating no starch was produced due to lack of CO2.

q: Respiration involves a number of chemical reactions that break down nutrient molecules, such as glucose, in living cells to release _____.
e: Respiration breaks down nutrient molecules like glucose in living cells to release energy.

q: There are two types of respiration: aerobic respiration and _____ respiration.
e: The two types of respiration are aerobic respiration and anaerobic respiration.

q: In prokaryotic organisms, aerobic respiration takes place in the _____.
e: In prokaryotic organisms, aerobic respiration takes place in the cytoplasm.

q: In eukaryotic organisms, aerobic respiration takes place in the _____ of cells.
e: In eukaryotic organisms, aerobic respiration takes place in the mitochondria of cells.

q: Anaerobic respiration takes place in the _____ of plant cells, animal cells and some microorganisms.
e: Anaerobic respiration takes place in the cytoplasm of plant cells, animal cells, and some microorganisms.

q: A mitochondrion has two membranes: an outer membrane and an _____.
e: A mitochondrion has two membranes: an outer membrane and an inner membrane.

q: Each membrane of a mitochondrion is made up of _____.
e: Each membrane of a mitochondrion is made up of a phospholipid bilayer.

q: The inner membrane of a mitochondrion has many folds called _____.
e: The inner membrane has many folds called cristae to increase surface area.

q: An increased surface area creates more space for more reactions to occur and increases the mitochondria's _____.
e: An increased surface area creates more space for reactions and increases the mitochondria's output.

q: The space between the outer and inner membranes is called the _____.
e: The space between the outer and inner membranes is called the inter-membrane space.

q: The space inside the inner membrane is called the _____.
e: The space inside the inner membrane is called the matrix.

q: Mitochondria can store _____, which maintains homeostasis of calcium levels in the cell.
e: Mitochondria can store calcium, which maintains homeostasis of calcium levels in the cell.

q: Mitochondria have roles in apoptosis, cell signaling, and _____ (heat production).
e: Mitochondria have roles in apoptosis, cell signaling, and thermogenesis (heat production).

q: In aerobic respiration, glucose is broken down to release energy in the presence of oxygen, forming carbon dioxide and _____.
e: In aerobic respiration, glucose is broken down in the presence of oxygen, forming carbon dioxide and water.

q: The balanced chemical equation for aerobic respiration releases _____ of energy.
e: The balanced chemical equation for aerobic respiration releases 2830 kJ of energy.

q: The balanced chemical equation for aerobic respiration produces _____ ATP.
e: Aerobic respiration produces 36-38 ATP molecules per glucose molecule.

q: Insect flight muscle has numerous mitochondria located between the _____.
e: Insect flight muscle has numerous mitochondria located between the muscle fibre to provide energy for contraction.

q: Liver cells have a high metabolism and have _____ mitochondria.
e: Liver cells have a high metabolism and therefore have many mitochondria.

q: The epithelial cells of the small intestine absorb glucose and other molecules by active transport, so have _____ numbers of mitochondria.
e: Epithelial cells of the small intestine have large numbers of mitochondria to provide energy for active transport.

q: In the experiment to demonstrate CO2 release in plants, a small glass tube containing 4 ml of _____ solution is hung into the conical flask.
e: A small glass tube containing potassium hydroxide (KOH) solution is hung into the conical flask to absorb CO2.

q: In the plant respiration experiment, the level of water rises in the glass tube because the CO2 gas is absorbed by _____ solution.
e: The CO2 gas evolved during respiration is absorbed by KOH solution, causing the water level to rise.

q: In the animal respiration experiment, air is drawn through the thistle funnel of _____ which absorbs all the atmospheric carbon dioxide.
e: Soda-lime is used to absorb all the atmospheric carbon dioxide before it reaches the animal.

q: In the animal respiration experiment, if the animal is producing carbon dioxide, the lime water in bottle B will turn _____.
e: If the animal is producing carbon dioxide, the lime water in bottle B will turn milky.

q: Anaerobic respiration is the breakdown of glucose into energy in the _____ of oxygen.
e: Anaerobic respiration is the breakdown of glucose into energy in the absence of oxygen.

q: Microorganisms such as yeast respire anaerobically by converting glucose into ethanol and _____.
e: Yeast respires anaerobically by converting glucose into ethanol and carbon dioxide.

q: The process of yeast converting glucose into ethanol and carbon dioxide is also termed as _____.
e: This process is also termed as alcohol fermentation.

q: The anaerobic respiration of glucose in yeast releases _____ of energy.
e: Anaerobic respiration in yeast releases 118 kJ of energy.

q: The anaerobic respiration of glucose in yeast produces _____ ATP.
e: Anaerobic respiration produces 2 ATP molecules.

q: During strenuous exercise, muscle tissue respires anaerobically to release energy, and glucose is broken down to _____ instead of carbon dioxide and water.
e: During strenuous exercise, glucose is broken down to lactic acid instead of carbon dioxide and water.

q: During vigorous exercise, lactic acid builds up in the muscles and blood, and causes the _____.
e: Lactic acid buildup in muscles and blood causes the oxygen debt.

q: The oxygen debt is removed during recovery by _____ respiration of lactic acid in the liver.
e: The oxygen debt is removed during recovery by aerobic respiration of lactic acid in the liver.

q: After exercise the heart continues to beat at a fast rate in order to transport lactic acid in the blood from the muscles to the _____.
e: The heart beats fast to transport lactic acid from the muscles to the liver.

q: Lactic acid must be broken down in the liver by breathing faster and deeper in order to supply more _____.
e: Breathing faster and deeper supplies more oxygen to break down lactic acid in the liver.

q: In the anaerobic respiration experiment with germinating seeds, the level of mercury in the test tube falls because of the collection of _____.
e: The level of mercury falls because of the collection of carbon dioxide gas produced by anaerobic respiration.

q: In the anaerobic respiration experiment, killed seeds are used as a _____.
e: Killed seeds are used as a control to show that the gas production is due to living processes.

q: ATP is a nucleotide that consists of three main structures: the nitrogenous base adenine, the pentose sugar ribose, and a chain of _____.
e: ATP consists of adenine, ribose, and a chain of three phosphate groups.

q: The ATP molecule is formed by bounding adenosine diphosphate to a phosphate group in _____ and absorbs energy released from glucose.
e: The ATP molecule is formed by bounding adenosine diphosphate to a phosphate group in the cytoplasm.

q: The energy released from ATP can be used for cell division and growth, synthesis of proteins, fats, vitamins, conduction of nerve impulses, maintenance of constant body temperature, and _____.
e: Energy from ATP is used for active transport of molecules and ions.

q: In the experiment to demonstrate the release of energy in germinating seeds, the soaked pea seeds are rinsed with 1% formalin for 5 minutes to kill the _____ on the surface.
e: Formalin is used to kill bacteria or fungi on the surface of the pea seeds to prevent their respiration from affecting the results.

q: In the energy release experiment, the temperature in the flask with the living seedlings will be _____ than in the control.
e: The temperature will be higher because heat energy is released during respiration of germinating seeds.

q: The products of one process (photosynthesis or respiration) are the _____ of the other.
e: Photosynthesis and cellular respiration are connected because the products of one process are the reactants of the other.

q: Photosynthesis makes the glucose that is used in cellular respiration to make _____.
e: Photosynthesis makes glucose, which is used in cellular respiration to make ATP.

q: While water is broken down to form oxygen during photosynthesis, in cellular respiration oxygen is combined with hydrogen to form _____.
e: In cellular respiration, oxygen is combined with hydrogen to form water.

q: Cellular respiration works best in the presence of _____.
e: Cellular respiration works best in the presence of oxygen (aerobic respiration).

q: Without oxygen, much less _____ would be produced during cellular respiration.
e: Without oxygen, much less ATP would be produced, as anaerobic respiration yields only 2 ATP compared to 36-38 ATP.

q: The exchange of carbon dioxide and oxygen during photosynthesis and cellular respiration worldwide helps to keep atmospheric oxygen and carbon dioxide at _____ levels.
e: This exchange helps to keep atmospheric oxygen and carbon dioxide at stable levels.

q: Photosynthesis occurs only in plants and _____.
e: Photosynthesis occurs only in plants and cyanobacteria.

q: Respiration occurs in _____ organisms.
e: Respiration occurs in all living organisms.

q: Photosynthesis takes place in the presence of light, while respiration takes place _____.
e: Respiration takes place throughout the day, independent of light.

q: In photosynthesis, light energy is fixed in the form of chemical energy and stored in _____.
e: In photosynthesis, light energy is fixed in the form of chemical energy and stored in carbohydrates.

q: In respiration, chemical energy stored in carbohydrates burns to release _____.
e: In respiration, chemical energy stored in carbohydrates burns to release energy.
